thesis: In a locked room where every external condition favoured surrender, Yusuf's first move was refuge in Allah rather than willpower, and the burhan that actually held him came from outside himself.

flags.quote: This last word — ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ — is one of the most theologically significant words in the surah, and it turns on a single vowel.
flags.issue: Section heading '3. Al-Mukhlasin — The Reading That Changes Everything' plus the 'The effort is theirs' / 'The effort is His' contrast makes the qira'at choice load-bearing. al-Tabari, the file's own principal source, explicitly rules the two readings equivalent: 'والصواب من القول في ذلك أن يقال: إنهما قراءتان معروفتان قد قرأ بهما جماعة كثيرة من القرأة، وهما متفقتا المعنى ... فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فهو للصوابِ مصيبٌ.' Worse for the framing, al-Jalalayn's base text prints the OTHER reading — '﴿إنّهُ مِن عِبادنا المُخْلِصِينَ﴾ فِي الطّاعَة وفِي قِراءَة بِفَتْحِ اللّام أيْ المُخْتارِينَ' — i.e. kasra as the text, fatha as the variant. The narrower claim 'The majority reading is mukhlasin — passive' IS grounded (al-Tabari: 'فقرأته عامة قرأة المدينة والكوفة ... بفتح اللام'), so the defect is the significance framing, not the count. The theological payload ('Allah saved him') is independently grounded in kadhalika linasrifa 'anhu and in al-Muyassar's 'وإنما أريناه ذلك؛ لندفع عنه', so the fix is to soften the heading and add al-Tabari's equivalence ruling — not to delete the section.

flags.quote: Al-Tabari runs through the reports — that Yusuf was shown the form of Ya'qub, or the form of the master of the house, or the warnings Allah revealed about *zina*
flags.issue: al-Tabari's second option is 'وجائز أن تكون صورة الملك' (and report 19089 from Ibn 'Abbas: 'أُرِيَ تمثالَ الملك'). الملك is the king or the angel — Ibn Kathir's edition renders it 'the image of an angel'. Neither source reads it as the 'Aziz / master of the house. Rendering it 'the form of the master of the house' silently imports an identification the sources do not make, and it does so in a file that elsewhere works hard to pin ownership on the 'Aziz. Fix: render as 'the form of the king (or the angel)' per the sources.

notes:
ALL THREE REPAIRS VERIFY. (i) Morphology: corpus 12:25:3:2 قَدَّتْ = 'PERF|VF:1' — plain Form I, and قُدَّ at 12:26:13:1 / 12:27:4:1 / 12:28:4:1 all 'PERF|VF:1|PASS'. The false Form II / 'intensive' inference is gone and the force is correctly relocated to the narrative (Ibn Kathir's 'tearing it so terribly that it fell off Yusuf's back' and al-Tabari's report that the tear landed at the back because Yusuf fled and she pursued — both confirmed in the fetched text). Neighbouring غَلَّقَتِ at 12:23:8:2 IS 'PERF|VF:2' — the intensive argument was correctly left intact. All 39 morphology comments in the file verify against the corpus, 0 mismatches. (ii) hamm ikhtilaf paragraph verifies line by line: al-Tabari 'إن الله جل ثناؤه أخبر عن همِّ يوسف وامرأة العزيز كل واحد منهما بصاحبه، لولا أن رأى يوسف برهان ربه'; al-Jalalayn 'وجَواب لَوْلا لَجامَعَها'; Ibn Kathir via al-Baghawi 'This is about the thoughts that cross the mind' + the Abu Hurayrah hadith + 'It was also reported that the Ayah means that Yusuf was about to beat her'; al-Muyassar's two-tier distinction 'ولقد مالت نفسها لفعل الفاحشة، وحدَّثت يوسفَ نفسُه حديث خطرات'. The paragraph REPORTS and does not adjudicate ('None of that is settled here'), carries an explicit tadabbur-vs-'ismah line ('That is a question of 'aqidah, argued by people trained for it, and a tadabbur is not where it is decided'), and openly owns its own lawla-fronted rendering ('That is the rendering used above in this file') instead of contradicting it. (iii) Ownership repair verifies: al-Jalalayn '﴿إنّهُ﴾ الَّذِي اشْتَرانِي ﴿رَبِّي﴾ سَيِّدِي', al-Tabari 'إن صاحبك وزوجك سيدي', and 12:25's سَيِّدَهَا. Grepped the whole file — no residual 'she was his owner' / 'he is her property'; every ownership sentence now reads 'the wife of the man who owns him' or equivalent.

SPECIFIC NEW-DEFECT CHECK — CLEARED, NOT AN OVERCLAIM. I checked all four editions individually on innahu rabbi before accepting 'all four commentaries consulted here read the hu as the 'Aziz'. Ibn Kathir: 'as they used to call the chief and master a Rabb, Yusuf said to her, your husband is my master'. al-Tabari: 'إن صاحبك وزوجك سيدي' plus chains 19002 al-Suddi 'سيدي', 19003 Ibn Abi Najih 'سيدي', 19007 Mujahid 'سيدي = يعني: زوج المرأة', 19008 Ibn Ishaq 'يعني: إطفير'. al-Muyassar: 'من خيانة سيدي الذي أحسن منزلتي وأكرمني فلا أخونه في أهله'. al-Jalalayn: 'الَّذِي اشْتَرانِي ... سَيِّدِي'. No edition is silent and none dissents — the breadth claim is true as written, and the named-chain detail ('Mujahid spells it out: sayyidi, meaning the woman's husband') is exact. The repair did NOT introduce a new overclaim here.

The two flags above are pre-existing, not repair-introduced. The mukhlasin one is the item the repairer raised and did not act on; I assess it as a real moderate defect because al-Tabari's equivalence ruling is nowhere in the file and the section is built on the contrast he denies. Countable claim 'The shirt appears four times in these seven verses' verifies exactly (root قمص at 12:25, 12:26, 12:27, 12:28 = 4).

thesis: Once punishment is visible the wronging soul would trade the whole earth to escape, but the ransom is impossible because everything already belongs to Allah, and the regret that arrives is concealment rather than tawbah.
notes:
REPAIR VERIFIED IN FULL, and the repair introduced no new overclaim. Every attribution in the rebuilt section matches the fetched text verbatim. al-Tabari: 'وأخفتْ رؤساء هؤلاء المشركين من وضعائهم وسفلتهم الندامةَ حين أبصرُوا عذاب الله قد أحاط بهم، وأيقنوا أنه واقع بهم' — the file's 'the chiefs of these mushrikin concealed their regret from their lowly ones and their followers, once they saw Allah's punishment closing around them and were certain it was landing on them' is an exact rendering. al-Jalalayn: '﴿وأَسَرُّوا النَّدامَة﴾ عَلى تَرْك الإيمان ﴿لَمّا رَأَوْا العَذاب﴾ أخْفاها رُؤَساؤُهُمْ عَنْ الضُّعَفاء الَّذِينَ أضَلُّوهُمْ مَخافَة التَّعْيِير' — the file carries both halves (the leaders/weak assignment AND the motive مخافة التعيير) and correctly adds that al-Jalalayn reads the regret itself as regret over abandoning faith (عَلى تَرْك الإيمان).

The two weaker editions are NOT overstated, which is exactly where these repairs usually break. al-Muyassar is described as 'plain and unassigned' — his text is 'وأخفى الذين ظلموا حسرتهم حين أبصروا عذاب الله واقعًا بهم جميعًا', which indeed assigns no concealer and no audience. Ibn Kathir is described as staying 'general too — they would feel the regret in their hearts' — his fetched rendering is 'they would feel in their hearts regret when they see the torment'. Neither is recruited into the leaders/followers reading, and the file's summary sentence is correctly scoped: 'So in the reading al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn carry...' — it names exactly the two editions that carry it. No 'all four', no unanimity claim, no unnamed remainder. This is how the breadth rule is supposed to be satisfied.

The reflective reading is now properly demoted: 'There is a second way to sit with the same verb, and it belongs to contemplation rather than to what the word itself states' — REFLECTION-FLAGGED, no longer asserted as what asarru means.

The new baynahum gloss is accurate and does not overclaim breadth: 'The commentators read baynahum in more than one width' (not 'all four'), then al-Tabari 'وقضى الله يومئذ بين الأتباع والرؤساء منهم بالعدل' = followers and leaders, and al-Jalalayn '﴿وقُضِيَ بَيْنهمْ﴾ بَيْن الخَلائِق' = all creation. Both exact; the two are correctly presented as differing in width rather than agreeing.

RE-CHECKED THE PREVIOUSLY VERIFIED MATERIAL AND IT STILL HOLDS. Section 4's divine-ownership argument tracks al-Tabari on 10:55 closely — he himself draws the ransom inference the file draws: 'فليس لهذا الكافر بالله يومئذٍ شيء يملكه فيفتدي به من عذاب ربّه، وإنما الأشياء كلها للذي إليه عقابه'. The qist reading is confirmed by al-Tabari 'بالعدل' and al-Jalalayn '﴿بِالقِسْطِ﴾ بِالعَدْلِ'; 'wa hum la yuzlamun' by al-Tabari 'لا يعاقب أحدًا منهم إلا بجريرته، ولا يأخذه بذنب أحدٍ' and al-Muyassar 'لأن الله تعالى لا يعاقب أحدًا إلا بذنبه'. The nadamah-is-not-tawbah distinction is consistent with al-Jalalayn's عَلى تَرْك الإيمان and the kufr context throughout. All 24 morphology comments verify against the corpus, 0 mismatches. No countable/absolute claims in the file require corpus arithmetic. Nothing for the human to action.

thesis: The muqtasimin were rejecters who partitioned revelation by denying part of it, and the passage turns that partitioning instinct into an accountable act the reader is warned by but not condemned as.
notes:
BOTH REPAIRS VERIFY, AND THE CRITICAL NUANCE IS DRAWN CORRECTLY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — this was the one I expected to break and it does not.

(i) Identification of the muqtasimin. Every attribution matches the fetched text. Ibn Kathir via al-Bukhari from Ibn 'Abbas: 'They are the People of the Book, who divided the Book into parts, believing in some of it, and rejecting some of it' — verbatim. The Ibn Ishaq report is carried accurately end to end (al-Walid bin al-Mughirah, al-Mawsim, the delegations, the run through soothsayer/crazy/poet, the landing on sorcerer, 'So they left having agreed upon that'). al-Jalalayn: '﴿عَلى المُقْتَسِمِينَ﴾ اليَهُود والنَّصارى'. al-Muyassar: '...من اليهود والنصارى وكفار قريش'. Ibn Kathir's oath-sense reading ('those who had made a pact to oppose, deny, and insult the Prophets', lined up with 27:49, 16:38, 14:44, 7:49) is reported accurately. al-Tabari's four-way spread and his refusal to choose are exact: 'فإذ لم يكن في التنزيل دلالة على أنه عُني به أحد الفرق الثلاثة دون الآخرين، ولا في خبر عن الرسول ﷺ، ولا في فطرة عقل'.

THE CRITICAL NUANCE — CLEARED. al-Tabari's generalization is 'وجب أن يكون مقتضيا بأن كلّ من اقتسم كتابا لله بتكذيب بعض وتصديق بعض ... فداخل في ذلك'. The operative word is تكذيب — declaring part of the Book a lie, a kufr category. The file names that word and builds the boundary on it: 'Notice the word he keeps returning to: takdhib, calling part of it a lie. That is the category he generalizes. He does not generalize it to a believer who accepts the whole Book and still obeys it unevenly.' It also correctly reports al-Tabari's own reason for the boundary at 15:91 — 'فمعلوم أنه لم يكن في مشركي قومه من يؤمن ببعض القرآن ويكفر ببعض، بل إنما كان قومه في أمره على أحد معنيين: إما مؤمن بجميعه، وإما كافر بجميعه' — rendered exactly. Crucially it does NOT blur in the OTHER direction either: line 181 keeps uneven obedience as a real fault ('That is a weakness to work on, and this passage can sharpen the will to work on it') before saying it is not the crime the ayah names. So the reader is neither threatened with a kufr verdict nor told they are safe regardless. That is the correct calibration and it is explicitly stated rather than left to inference. Adab closer present: 'This is a tadabbur, not a ruling, and nothing here judges anyone's faith.'

(ii) Elided object of anzalna supplied as PUNISHMENT — verified in all three editions the file cites. al-Jalalayn writes it into the verse: '﴿كَما أنْزَلْنا﴾ العَذاب'. al-Tabari: 'مثل الذي أنزل الله تعالى من البلاء والعقاب على الذين اقتسموا القرآن، فجعلوه عِضين'. al-Muyassar: 'ومنذركم أن يصيبكم العذاب، كما أنزله الله على الذين قسَّموا القرآن'. The file names exactly these three and does not claim the fourth.

(iii) 'idin derivation — the file now hedges correctly and matches the corpus. Corpus 15:91:4:1 عِضِينَ = 'ROOT:عضو', and the file says so explicitly ('The Quranic corpus files the word under the root '-d-w, the limb reading') while reporting that al-Tabari's own preference leans toward the slander sense — which is true ('عَضَهُوا القرآن ... قذفهموه بالباطل') — and closing with al-Tabari's own reconciliation, rendered exactly: 'فهما متقاربان في المعنى' → 'are close to each other in meaning'. Both derivations al-Tabari lays out (جمع عِضة from العَضْه/البَهْت, and جمع عُضْو from التعضية 'كما تُعَضى الجَزُور والشاة') appear in the file including the slaughtered-animal image. All 9 morphology comments verify, 0 mismatches. Nothing for the human to action.

thesis: The honours Allah gives — the Night Journey, scripture, rescue, restored power — are meant to deepen servanthood and gratitude, and when a people forget that, consequence returns; the address is universal, not confined to one community.

flags.quote: This passage names no nation, no century, and no people alive today.
flags.issue: Absolute claim that fails literally: the passage DOES name a nation — بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ at 17:2 and again at 17:4 (both quoted in the file's own ayah blocks), plus Musa and Nuh. From context the sentence plainly means 'the passage supplies no identification of the INVADERS' — the preceding sentence is about the tafsir identifications and the next one names 17:5 and 17:7 — and the load-bearing clause 'no people alive today' is true and is the protective part. But this is the single most adversarially-quotable sentence in the file's most adversarially-quotable section, and it should not contain a literal inaccuracy an opponent can lift. Fix is one clause: 'This passage names none of these invaders, no century, and no people alive today.'

notes:
THE ADDED SECTION DOES NOT IMPORT ISRA'ILIYYAT AND NAMES NO MODERN PARTY. Both critical checks CLEAR.

No identification is stated as settled. Every one is carried as an attributed, conflicting report — 'one from Ibn 'Abbas naming Jalut, one from Sa'id ibn Jubayr naming Sennacherib out of Ashur and Nineveh, one from Mujahid saying the first episode was a Persian scouting party' — and the section's own conclusions are 'These are not variations on one account. They are different accounts' and 'The identifications stay where the tafsir tradition left them: unsettled, and not needed.' Even al-Jalalayn's version is reported with distance built in: 'writes the Jalut version into the verse as though it were settled.' Note also what the section conspicuously omits: the fetched Ibn Kathir text contains the charged narrative material (the Nebuchadnezzar campaign, the censer, 'he killed seventy thousand'), and Ibn Kathir's own aside about 'when (the Jews) committed transgression and aggression' — none of it is reproduced. The only appearance of 'Jewish' in the whole file is the neutral technical gloss of Isra'iliyyat as 'reports taken from Jewish sources', which is Ibn Kathir's own framing verbatim ('Many Isra'iliyyat (reports from Jewish sources) were narrated about this').

Modern-mapping check: grepped for Jew/Zion/Palestin/Israeli/Gaza/occupation/settler/conflict/state-of — zero hits outside that one definitional gloss. No modern people, state, or contemporary conflict is named, alluded to, or mapped onto, even by implication. The file goes further and forecloses the move outright: 'Anyone who reaches for a headline to fill in 17:5 or 17:7 is doing the very thing Ibn Kathir declined to do, and with far worse sources', plus the adab closer 'not a ruling on history and not a judgment on any community.' The universality anchor does the real protective work — it turns the mirror onto the reader rather than onto any group.

Attributions all verify against the fetched text. Ibn Kathir's withholding statement is exact: 'The earlier and later commentators differed over the identity of these invaders. Many Isra'iliyyat ... were narrated about this, but I did not want to make this book too long by mentioning them, because some of them are fabricated ... and others may be true, but we have no need of them ... What Allah has told us in His Book (the Qur'an) is sufficient.' His grading of the Musayyib/Nebuchadnezzar report is exact — the text says 'This report is Sahih from Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib', and the file says 'a report he grades as authentic'. al-Tabari's split marker is exact: 'ثم اختلف أهل التأويل في الذين عنى الله بقوله ﴿أُولي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾'. The three al-Tabari reports check out individually: Jalut ('فقال بعضهم: كان الذي بعث الله عليهم في المرّة الأولى جالوت', chained to Ibn 'Abbas); Sennacherib ('سمعت سعيد بن جبير ... بعث الله ... عليهم في المرّة الأولى سنحاريب من أهل أثور ونينوى'); Mujahid ('من جاءهم من فارس يتجسسون أخبارهم، ويسمعون حديثهم ... ثم رجعت فارس ولم يكن قتال'). al-Jalalayn's Jalut gloss is there in the verse as described: 'فَبَعَثَ عَلَيْهِمْ جالُوت وجُنُوده'. These are genuinely incompatible, so the section's central point is sound.

17:3 UNIVERSALITY ANCHOR VERIFIED, including the two named followers. al-Tabari: 'وعنى بالذرية: جميع من احتجّ عليه جلّ ثناؤه بهذا القرآن من أجناس الأمم، عربهم وعجمهم من بني إسرائيل وغيرهم، وذلك أنّ كلّ من على الأرض من بني آدم، فهم من ذرية من حمله الله مع نوح في السفينة' — the file's rendering is exact on both halves. Mujahid: 'من بني إسرائيل وغيرهم' — and the file's countable claim 'says the same in four words' is literally correct (من / بني / إسرائيل / وغيرهم = 4). Qatadah: 'والناس كلهم ذرّية من أنجى الله في تلك السفينة' — the file's 'and all people are the descendants of those Allah saved in that ship' is exact.

RUBRIC CHECK 2 RE-RUN OVER THE WHOLE FILE. Countable/absolute claims extracted and checked: 'in four words' (verified, 4); 'The Quran does not name the invaders in 17:5' (verified — 17:5 reads عِبَادًا لَّنَا أُو۟لِى بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ, no name); 'It does not date the two episodes' (verified); 'twice over' / marratayn (verified); 'a report he grades as authentic' (verified); 'Not His prophet. Not His messenger. Not even his blessed personal name' (verified — 17:1 reads بِعَبْدِهِ). The three superlatives are all hedged and therefore not falsifiable claims: 'one of the great Quranic calibrations', 'one of the starkest historical warnings in the Quran', 'among the most staggering honors ever given to a human being in this world' — the third is the minor superlative previously flagged; 'among the most' keeps it inside the rubric, so I did not fail it, but a human may still want it trimmed. All 82 morphology comments verify against the corpus, 0 mismatches. The single failing claim is the 'names no nation' sentence above — a one-clause fix, no restructuring needed.
